question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Face-saving measure

options.text: A way to protect the face from injury

explanation: Face-saving measure = इज़्ज़त बचाने का उपाय। Example: The apology was only a face-saving measure.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To flog a dead horse

options.text: To win a race by effort
To waste effort on a lost cause

explanation: Flog a dead horse = ऐसे मामले पर मेहनत करना जिसका नतीजा न निकले। Example: Arguing with him is like flogging a dead horse.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Get wind of something

options.text: To learn about a secret or private matter

explanation: Get wind of something = भनक लग जाना। Example: The press got wind of the scandal.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To give a wide berth

options.text: To keep a safe distance from

explanation: Give a wide berth = किसी से दूरी बनाए रखना। Example: Give that dog a wide berth.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Go against the grain

options.text: To act contrary to one's principles or nature
To cut wood the right way

explanation: Go against the grain = स्वभाव या सिद्धांतों के विपरीत काम करना। Example: Telling lies goes against the grain for him.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Go the extra mile
explanation: Go the extra mile = अपेक्षा से अधिक प्रयास करना। Example: She went the extra mile to help the new student.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To hang in the balance
explanation: Hang in the balance = अधर में लटकना, नतीजा अनिश्चित। Example: The patient's life hung in the balance.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To have too many irons in the fire

options.text: To be involved in too many activities at once

explanation: Too many irons in the fire = एक साथ बहुत से कामों में उलझे रहना। Example: With four projects, he has too many irons in the fire.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Hit below the belt
explanation: Hit below the belt = अनुचित तरीके से वार करना। Example: Mocking his poverty was hitting below the belt.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Hold a candle to

options.text: To light a lamp for someone
To be as good as someone else

explanation: Hold a candle to = किसी की बराबरी कर पाना। Example: No singer can hold a candle to her.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Keep an eye on
explanation: Keep an eye on = नज़र रखना। Example: Please keep an eye on my bag.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Leave it on the back burner

options.text: To postpone a task or project

explanation: Leave on the back burner = किसी काम को बाद के लिए टाल देना। Example: The plan was left on the back burner.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Off the cuff
explanation: Off the cuff = बिना तैयारी के, तुरंत। Example: He gave an off-the-cuff reply.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: On the ball
explanation: On the ball = सतर्क और सक्षम। Example: Our new clerk is really on the ball.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Straight from the horse's mouth

options.text: From the most reliable or primary source

explanation: Straight from the horse's mouth = सबसे विश्वसनीय या मूल स्रोत से। Example: I heard it straight from the horse's mouth.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Through thick and thin

options.text: Under all conditions, both good and bad

explanation: Through thick and thin = हर हाल में। Example: True friends stay together through thick and thin.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To tie oneself up in knots
explanation: Tie oneself up in knots = बुरी तरह उलझ जाना या घबरा जाना। Example: She tied herself up in knots before the interview.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Upset the apple cart

options.text: To ruin a carefully planned arrangement

explanation: Upset the apple cart = बना-बनाया खेल बिगाड़ना। Example: His late objection upset the apple cart.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Want to curl up and die

options.text: To feel extreme embarrassment or shame

explanation: Curl up and die = शर्म से ज़मीन में गड़ जाना। Example: I wanted to curl up and die when my phone rang in class.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To weather the storm

options.text: To face difficulties bravely and survive them

explanation: Weather the storm = मुश्किलों का बहादुरी से सामना कर पार पाना। Example: The company weathered the storm of recession.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A red-letter day
explanation: A red-letter day = यादगार शुभ दिन। Example: The day I joined the army was a red-letter day for me.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A sight for sore eyes
explanation: A sight for sore eyes = आँखों को सुकून देने वाला दृश्य। Example: After a year abroad, my brother was a sight for sore eyes.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder

options.text: Beauty is a matter of personal taste

explanation: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder = सुंदरता देखने वाले की नज़र में होती है। Example: He loves that old painting; beauty is in the eye of the beholder.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Blaze a trail

options.text: To be the first to do something new
To set a forest on fire

explanation: Blaze a trail = नई राह बनाना। Example: Kalpana Chawla blazed a trail for Indian women in space.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Dance to someone's tune
explanation: Dance to someone's tune = किसी के इशारों पर नाचना। Example: He refuses to dance to his boss's tune.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Drop the ball
explanation: Drop the ball = लापरवाही से चूक जाना। Example: The clerk dropped the ball and lost the file.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Hold all the aces

options.text: To be in a very strong position

explanation: Hold all the aces = हर तरह से भारी पड़ना। Example: With the funds and the votes, she holds all the aces.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Lord it over

options.text: To act in a superior, bossy way

explanation: Lord it over = रौब जमाना। Example: Don't lord it over your juniors.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Play into someone's hands
explanation: Play into someone's hands = अनजाने में विरोधी का फ़ायदा करा देना। Example: By losing his temper, he played into his rival's hands.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Rule the roost
explanation: Rule the roost = हुक्म चलाना, सर्वेसर्वा होना। Example: In that house, the grandmother rules the roost.
